title: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease

steps.tx: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (**ADPKD**) is caused by loss-of-function mutations in **PKD1** (encoding **polycystin-1**, chromosome 16p13.3) in approximately **78%** of families, or **PKD2** (encoding **polycystin-2**, chromosome 4q21) in **15%**. PKD1 mutations confer significantly earlier clinical onset and more rapid progression to ESKD (mean age **58** years versus **79** years in PKD2).
steps.say: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease is caused by loss-of-function mutations in PKD1 encoding polycystin-1 in approximately 78% of families, or PKD2 encoding polycystin-2 in 15%. PKD1 mutations confer significantly earlier clinical onset and more rapid progression to ESKD, with a mean age of 58 years versus 79 years in PKD2.

steps.tx: The Unified **Pei-Ravine ultrasound criteria** establish definitive diagnosis in at-risk individuals with a positive family history: age **15** to **39** years requires >= **3** unilateral or bilateral cysts; age **40** to **59** requires >= **2** cysts in each kidney; and age >= **60** requires >= **4** cysts per kidney, with fewer than two cysts excluding disease in patients aged 40 and older.
steps.say: The Unified Pei-Ravine ultrasound criteria establish definitive diagnosis in at-risk individuals with a positive family history: age 15 to 39 years requires 3 or more unilateral or bilateral cysts; age 40 to 59 requires 2 or more cysts in each kidney; and age 60 and older requires 4 or more cysts per kidney, with fewer than two cysts excluding disease in patients aged 40 and older.

steps.tx: The **Mayo imaging classification** predicts renal disease progression by calculating height-adjusted **total kidney volume** (**htTKV**) and patient age to stratify patients into Classes 1A through 1E. Classes **1C**, 1D, and **1E** denote rapid progressors with estimated htTKV growth rates exceeding 3% per year, identifying candidates who derive substantial benefit from disease-modifying therapies.

steps.tx: The selective **vasopressin V2 receptor antagonist** **Tolvaptan** blocks basolateral V2 receptors on principal cells, suppressing intracellular **cAMP** and inhibiting protein kinase A-driven cyst epithelial cell proliferation and fluid secretion. In the pivotal **TEMPO 3:4** and REPRISE trials, tolvaptan significantly slowed htTKV growth and attenuated the annual rate of eGFR decline.

steps.tx: Intracranial **berry aneurysms** of the circle of Willis develop in approximately **10%** of unselected ADPKD patients, with prevalence rising to **20%** to **25%** among patients with a positive **family history** of intracranial aneurysm or subarachnoid hemorrhage. Presymptomatic screening using magnetic resonance angiography (**MRA**) without gadolinium is strongly recommended in high-risk pedigrees.

left.title: Clinical Sequence
points: ADPKD with family history of aneurysm
Screening non-contrast MRA of circle of Willis
Neurosurgical coiling or surveillance if detected

steps.tx: The most frequent extrarenal manifestation of ADPKD is **polycystic liver disease**, occurring in over 80% of affected adults. Severe hepatic involvement is markedly exacerbated by **female sex**, multiple past **pregnancies**, and exogenous **estrogen exposure**, driven by hepatic cyst cholangiocyte proliferation and local fluid secretion.

steps.tx: Differentiating an acute **infected renal cyst** from acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis requires meticulous imaging. While conventional ultrasound and CT often appear ambiguous, **FDG-PET/CT** exhibits high sensitivity and specificity by demonstrating intense focal metabolic tracer avidity within the inflamed cyst wall, guiding prolonged targeted lipid-soluble antimicrobial therapy.

right.title: Acute Intracystic Hemorrhage
points: Sudden severe flank pain and hematuria
Absence of fever and septic markers
High attenuation (> 50 HU) on unenhanced CT
Managed with bed rest and analgesia

steps.tx: In the landmark **HALT-PKD** clinical trial, intensive blood pressure control targeting **95/60** to **110/75** mmHg using an **ACE inhibitor** or ARB significantly slowed the rate of total kidney volume growth and produced greater reductions in left ventricular mass index compared to standard blood pressure targets (**120/70** to **130/80** mmHg).
